articles.title: 86-year-old sailor and his dog rescued 460 miles off California after disappearing during a 5,000-mile Pacific voyage for more than two months
articles.summary: An 86-year-old sailor and his dog have been rescued more than two months after disappearing during a voyage across the Pacific Ocean.
articles.body: An 86-year-old sailor and his dog have been rescued more than two months after disappearing during a voyage across the Pacific Ocean. The pair were aboard the sailboat Willow Wind, travelling from Astoria, Oregon, to Pago Pago in American Samoa, when contact was lost on August 20. The U.S. Coast Guard was alerted that the sailor was overdue on October 24, before an emergency beacon from his vessel triggered a search three days later. A Coast Guard aircraft eventually located the disabled sailboat about 460 miles off San Diego, leading to a rescue involving merchant mariners and Coast Guard crews.86-year-old sailor and his dog disappeared during a Pacific voyageThe sailor had set out from Astoria, Oregon, aboard the Willow Wind with his dog, bound for Pago Pago in American Samoa. The planned journey covered roughly 5,000 miles across the Pacific. According to PEOPLE, nobody had heard from the pair since August 20. Authorities were not immediately aware of their situation, and the sailor was eventually reported overdue on October 24. The Coast Guard then began coordinating a search for the missing vessel and its occupants. The case involved an elderly sailor travelling a long ocean route far from the California coast.Emergency beacon helped rescuers locate the missing sailboatA breakthrough came on October 27, when an emergency transmitter registered to the Willow Wind sent an alert. The Coast Guard responded by deploying aircraft and the cutter Robert Ward, while nearby vessels were also asked to assist. A C-27 Spartan aircraft from Coast Guard Air Station Sacramento eventually located the sailboat about 460 miles off San Diego. The discovery came more than two months after the sailor and his dog had last been heard from. The vessel was still drifting at sea, giving rescuers a precise location from which to organise the recovery operation.Rough seas initially prevented the sailor and dog from being rescuedThe motor vessel Grand Orion reached the Willow Wind early on October 28, but difficult sea conditions initially made it too dangerous for the crew to bring the sailor and his dog aboard. Later that day, conditions allowed the merchant vessel's crew to complete the rescue at about 5:36 p.m. The Willow Wind had damaged sails and was left adrift after the pair were taken to safety. The successful recovery came after a lengthy period without communication and followed a coordinated response involving aircraft, a Coast Guard cutter and commercial vessels.Coast Guard helicopter flew the pair back to CaliforniaAs per Fox News, the rescue operation continued the following morning when a Coast Guard helicopter crew hoisted the sailor and his dog from the Grand Orion. The vessel was then about 170 miles west of Ventura, California. The pair were transported to San Diego, where the sailor was taken to Scripps Mercy Hospital for medical evaluation. PEOPLE reported that emergency medical personnel found him weak and having difficulty walking, but he had no major injuries. The Coast Guard did not provide further details about the dog's condition. The rescue therefore ended with both survivors safely removed from the disabled sailboat.Damaged sails left the 86-year-old sailor stranded far offshoreThe condition of the Willow Wind appears to have played a major role in the emergency. By the time rescuers located the vessel, its sails were damaged, and it was drifting in the Pacific. The boat was ultimately left behind after the sailor and his dog were transferred to the Grand Orion. The distance from the California coast also complicated the response, with the vessel initially located about 460 miles from San Diego. The rescue required coordination between Coast Guard aircraft, a cutter and commercial mariners already operating in the region.Coast Guard stresses importance of emergency communication at seaCoast Guard Cmdr. Jason Nguyen said the successful rescue highlighted the value of emergency communication equipment and having a float plan so someone onshore knows a vessel's intended route. In this case, the emergency transmitter aboard the Willow Wind ultimately provided the crucial alert that allowed authorities to locate the missing sailor and his dog. The pair had gone without contact for more than two months before the beacon signal was received.
